subject: artifacts/check-claims.py and METHOD.CLAIM-STATUS-INTEGRITY

independence.method: Reproduced the live false negative, measured probe coverage, then injected only the missing location probe in memory to isolate whether the engine or its coverage was responsible.
independence.differentInstrument: This is a negative-control and coverage test against the live corpus, not a review of prior repair citations.

priorFindingDisposition.B-ARCH-01: CONFIRMED. The candidate completeness claim is presented under architecture/10's SEALED method-rules container, and the normal checker reports clean.
priorFindingDisposition.B-ARCH-02: CONFIRMED. The normal checker also reports clean while architecture/07, /09, and /11 name superseded D9/R1 binding versions.

resolves.B-CSI-01: OPEN-BLOCKER: CHK-1 silently skips home and restatement locations without _probe; 29 of 30 registered claims currently lack one.
resolves.B-CSI-02: OPEN-BLOCKER: the self-test proves engine behavior only after supplying a probe and cannot fail when live coverage is absent.
resolves.B-CSI-03: OPEN-BLOCKER: CHK-3 is a three-claim signature allowlist and no check compares prose artifact/version references with current bindingArtifact values.

evidence: METHOD.CLAIM-STATUS-INTEGRITY is CANDIDATE in the register
its home and remedy restatement are under architecture/10 line 16's SEALED marker with no inline candidate mark
the claim has no _probe, so CHK-1a uses offset -1 and CHK-1 uses offset None, then silently continues
the live register has 30 claims but only ARCH.RETENTION-TIERS has _probe
adding only a METHOD.CLAIM-STATUS-INTEGRITY probe in memory makes the same checker emit two CHK-1 findings
findings.impact: The mechanism advertised as preventing local prose from creating unauthorized global status claims is blind to almost the entire registered inventory, including its own completeness claim.
findings.requiredChange: Make location coverage mandatory: every markdown home and restatement must resolve through a stable explicit claim marker or exact registered anchor. Missing/ambiguous anchors must be findings, never skips. Then repair the live METHOD clause inline or weaken its container.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A clean checker run after deleting every _probe would have to fail with explicit coverage findings for the unresolved homes/restatements.

evidence: self_test hardcodes _probe for its synthetic C-X restatement
it does not include a claim whose home/restatement lacks a probe
it checks only that three expected prefixes appear, not that every registered location was examined
both self-test and live check pass while the live METHOD false negative remains
findings.impact: The regression suite proves a supported happy path but not the dominant live failure mode: omitted coverage. Passing it creates stronger confidence than the tested property warrants.
findings.requiredChange: Add negative controls for absent, stale, duplicate, and wrong-location anchors; assert checked-location count equals required-location count; make the self-test fail if any target is skipped.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A coverage assertion outside the displayed checker that is mandatory in the canonical command and fails on the current 29 unprobed claims.

evidence: SIGNATURES contains patterns for only ARCH.BASELINE.PRODUCER-DERIVED, ARCH.IDENTITY.LATEST, and C-1
architecture/07 still calls v1.1 binding and v1.2 schema-complete; architecture/09 names v1.4; architecture/11 inventories v1.2
R-1's current bindingArtifact is v1.3 while architecture/11 inventories v1
findings.impact: Status can be correct in the register while readers are directed to superseded binding objects and obsolete review states. The checker does not enforce its advertised document-set consistency.
findings.requiredChange: Represent artifact references as structured claim metadata or machine-readable claim tags in prose, then verify every current-binding restatement names the register's bindingArtifact and status. Replace the hand-picked signature allowlist with inventory-derived coverage.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A separate mandatory checker that rejects the cited live stale references and is part of the canonical four-check command set.

knownLimitations: This review demonstrates coverage and version false negatives; it does not design the final stable claim-marker syntax.
It does not assert that every one of the 29 unprobed claims is currently mis-presented, only that the checker cannot establish that they are not.
The in-memory probe test used the checker's own public check/docs functions and made no repository mutation.
